title: Microgravity flammability boundary for PMMA rods in axial stagnation flow: Experimental results and energy balance analyses (2017)
summary: Not read. By its title the Olson and Ferkul BASS-II PMMA rod flammability-boundary paper (axial stagnation flow, ISS and drop tower), which PSI-62 uses as benchmark data; the record uses the 2015 NTRS conference version 20150008961 instead.
notes: No free full text or abstract found: OpenAlex and Crossref carry no abstract, Semantic Scholar reports it elided by the publisher, the publisher page (ScienceDirect/Wiley/Springer/T&F) refuses automated access, and no NTRS, OSTI, PMC or repository copy was found. NTRS search by title found only the 2015-2017 related conference papers.

title: Radiative flamelet generated manifolds for solid fuel flame spread in microgravity (2023)
summary: 2-D detailed-chemistry, coupled-radiation model of opposed-flow flame spread over thin PMMA, compared with BASS spread rates for a 2 cm wide, 100 um slab at 20.6% O2; it over-predicts spread rate by a factor 1.5-2.7 in some regions, most in the kinetic regime. Coupled radiative FGMs built from 1-D flamelets reproduce most of the 2-D chemical states; a-priori OH errors 3.0, 4.5 and 13.1% and CO errors 4.9, 6.0 and 5.2% at 3.75, 10 and 40 cm/s. Each 2-D case takes 1-3 days.

items.claim: The BASS comparison shown is at a single far-field oxygen level (20.6% by volume) over flow speeds 3.75-40 cm/s, not over a range of oxygen levels as the record (from the abstract) states; the model over-predicts BASS spread rates by 1.5-2.7x in some regions.
items.quote: the predicted flame spread rates from the model over predict the experiments by a factor 1.5 − 2.7 in some regions.

items.claim: BASS benchmark geometry: 2 cm wide, 100 um thick PMMA slab, far-field O2 20.6%.
items.quote: Figure 8 shows a comparison between the model predicted and the experimentally measured flame spread rates from the NASA BASS missions for a 2 cm wide, 100 μm thick slab of PMMA with a far field volumetric
oxygen concentration of 20.6%. Also compared are model predictions made by Bhattacharjee et. al.

items.claim: Over-prediction is largest in the kinetic (high-flow) regime; attributed to the simplified transport model and not solving the full momentum equations.
items.quote: The model over predicts the flame spread rate in almost all cases, especially in the kinetic regime.
Average errors for OH are 3.0%, 4.5%, and 13.1%, while CO errors are 4.9%, 6.0%, and 5.2% for the 3.75, 10, 40 cm/s cases respectively.

items.claim: Quasi-coupled fuel boundary critical; differences near attachment from flame-wall interaction and curvature.
items.quote: Differences between the 2D model data and the CR-FGM’s are then identified to be from flame-wall interactions and curved flame structure effects.

notes: Accepted manuscript on OSTI (purl 2576508, Elsevier user licence). The paper models opposed-flow spread; the PSI title says 'concurrent flame spread'. Record finding updated, old wording kept in gaps.

title: Theoretical estimates of flammability bounds for thin condensed fuel diffusion flames in microgravity using detailed models of chemistry and radiation (2023)
summary: Thin-flame theory with a Damkohler-based progress variable plus 1-D numerical models (planar and spherical; global one-step and 67-species detailed MMA chemistry) give U-shaped flammability maps compared with the Olson-Ferkul PMMA rod data (drop tower and ISS BASS). Predicted minimum O2 is 11.1% (global chemistry) and 12.6% (detailed), 2.4 and 0.9 percentage points below the experimental minimum; spherical geometry lowers it slightly (to 10.92% and 12.3%).

items.claim: Predicted minimum oxygen concentration 11.1% (global chemistry, both models), 2.4 points below the experimental value.
items.quote: For the global chemistry model, both of the minimum oxygen concentrations predicted by the numerical and thin flame theory are 11.1%. However the thin flame predicts this to occur at a larger χ. These are both 2.4% lower than the experimentally observed values.

items.claim: With detailed chemistry the predicted minimum is 12.6%, 0.9 points below experiment.
items.quote: both the minimum oxygen concentrations for the thin flame and numerical model occur at 12.6%, which is 0.9% lower than the experiments.

items.claim: Spherical vs planar geometry lowers the predicted minimum O2 slightly; high-strain bound insensitive to geometry.
items.quote: decreasing from 11.1% to 10.92% for the global case and from 12.6% to 12.3% for the detailed case.

items.claim: Qualitative agreement with microgravity data; radiative bound captured.
items.quote: The results show the newly developed analytics capture the radiative extinction bound compared to the numerical model and qualitatively agrees with microgravity data.

notes: Accepted manuscript on OSTI (purl 2417649). Minimum-O2 predictions added to the record as a new finding. Acknowledges NASA grant 80NSSC20K0426, the grant in the PSI-62 record, so the 2023 papers are confirmed as products of this grant. The experimental minimum (about 13.5% implied) is from Olson and Ferkul, not stated directly here.

title: Two-color pyrometry based flame to fuel surface radiative heat flux diagnostic using flamelets
summary: Two-colour flamelet-manifold diagnostic for DSLR images applied to upward flame spread over a vertical PMMA slab at standard conditions (1 g). Accounting for self-absorption gives a maximum soot volume fraction of 7 ppm and a peak flame-to-surface radiative flux of 42 kW/m2 about 3 cm above the flame base. Not applied to BASS imagery.

items.claim: Demonstrated on 1 g upward flame spread only.
items.quote: The experiment is conducted at STP

items.claim: Normal-gravity results: max soot 7 ppm, peak radiative flux 42 kW/m2.
items.quote: The maximum soot volume fraction is 7 ppm

notes: Accepted manuscript on OSTI (purl 1772898). Funded by NSF 1704447 and NASA 80NSSC20K0426.
